## The equation-of-state limiter: two passes, floors and marks {#sec-ch08-eoslimiter}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5 (chengcli/snapy)
sources: OUTLINE.md 8.5, 8.6 and 8.7, merged

### Summary

The equation of state floors the state in two passes. The conserved pass zeroes NaNs, floors the dry density
and floors the total energy at the kinetic energy plus the internal energy of a temperature floor. The
primitive pass floors density and pressure and clamps the species fractions at zero. A repair in the interior
sets a mark that the redo detector of @sec-ch08-redo reads.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Clamp the state back into the admissible set: two floor passes and a NaN repair, each setting a mark.

**Data.** In: `hydro_u` (conserved pass) or `hydro_w` (primitive pass). Out: the same tensor floored in place; two marks.

**Placement.** Inside the equation-of-state conversions of every stage; the marks are read by `check_redo`.

**Activation.** `equation-of-state/limiter: true` (default false); the card's floors default to $10^{-6}$, $10^{-3}$ and 20 K.

**Guarantee / limits.** None: a clamp invents mass or energy and nothing removes it; the two conserved floors do not commute.

**Evidence.** `[C1]`, `[C2]`, `[C4]`, `[C5]` of `floors_check`; the repair cases of `test_forcing.<b>`.
:::

Local symbols: $\rho_{\mathrm{fl}}$ [kg m$^{-3}$], $p_{\mathrm{fl}}$ [Pa] and $T_{\mathrm{fl}}$ [K] are the density, pressure and
temperature floors; $\rho e(T_{\mathrm{fl}})$ [J m$^{-3}$] is the internal energy density of a cell at the temperature
floor. $E$, $\rho_i$, $\mathbf v$ and $V_i$ are NOTATION.md's.

### Derivation

There is no derivation for a floor. What there is instead are three facts about the operator that a
reader needs and that are easy to get wrong, and the check establishes each separately.

*The passes do not commute.* The conserved pass floors the dry density first. It then floors the total energy at the
kinetic energy plus the internal energy of a temperature floor. That internal energy is computed from the density the
previous statement has already clamped. `[C1]` reorders the two statements and measures the result: on three thousand
random states straddling the floors, the energy differs in $2862$ of them, by up to $1.33\times10^{4}$. The order is
not incidental.

*The floors are repairs, not conservative operations.* A clamp can only add. `[C2]` measures how much:
on four thousand cells straddling the floors the passes add $4.736\times10^{-4}$ of dry mass and
$1.294\times10^{2}$ of total energy, both strictly positive. Nothing anywhere in the code removes it
again. This is the sense in which snapy guarantees no positivity of density or pressure: it repairs
them, at a cost it does not track.

*The two passes floor different things.* `[C5]` separates them. The primitive pass floors density and
pressure and clamps species mass fractions at zero; it has no energy row and applies no temperature
floor. The conserved pass has no pressure row and floors energy through the temperature floor instead.
Reading either as the other applied to different variables is wrong.

The marks are the link to the redo machinery. `[C4]` checks the cases that matter. An untouched state marks nothing, a
density below the floor sets the patch mark, and a NaN sets the NaN mark. The same repair outside the interior marks
nothing at all, because a repair in a ghost cell must not force a block to redo its step.

### Numerical method

The conserved pass is `cons`
({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}) and runs in a fixed order.
NaNs are zeroed and marked at
{{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}, the dry density is clamped
at {{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}. The energy is clamped at
{{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}} to the kinetic energy plus
the internal energy of the temperature floor. The kinetic energy there is built from the momentum raised with the
cell's own metric, so the floor is correct on a curved grid and not only in Cartesian.

The primitive pass is `prim` ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_primitive_limiter_ >}}): NaNs, the density floor at
{{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_primitive_limiter_ >}}, the species clamp at {{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_primitive_limiter_ >}} and
the pressure floor at {{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_primitive_limiter_ >}}.

The floor values are YAML keys with defaults at `density_floor` ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}): a density
floor of $10^{-6}$, a pressure floor of $10^{-3}$ and a temperature floor of $20$ K. They are absolute
numbers in the deck's own units, not fractions of anything, so whether they are conservative or
catastrophic depends on the scaling of the problem.

The marks are a two-element device-side boolean buffer, reset at `reset_limiter_marks`
({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::reset_limiter_marks >}}) and read by the redo detector of
@sec-ch08-redo. Entry one is the NaN mark and entry zero the patch mark, set at `limiter_marks_`
({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}). They are set by comparing
the density and energy rows against a copy taken before the floors.

**Why this order, and what a floor costs.** Three facts of the code.

1. The energy floor is $E \ge \tfrac12\rho\lvert\mathbf v\rvert^2 + \rho e(T_{\mathrm{fl}})$ with $\rho e$ computed from the density the previous statement has already
   clamped ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}), so the two
   floors do not commute; `[C1]` measures the difference.
2. A clamp can only add: the invented mass is $\sum_i \max(\rho_{\mathrm{fl}} - \rho_i, 0)\,V_i \ge 0$ and likewise for the
   energy; `[C2]` measures both strictly positive and nothing removes them.
3. The marks compare the interior rows against a copy taken before the floors. A repair in a ghost cell marks nothing
   and cannot force a block to redo its step.

: Code map of the equation-of-state limiter. {#tbl-ch08-eoslimiter-code}

**How to use it.** All four keys live in the equation-of-state block
({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}):

```yaml
dynamics:
  equation-of-state:
    limiter: true
    density-floor: 1.e-6       # the reader's default
    pressure-floor: 1.e-3
    temperature-floor: 20.
```

An options struct built in C++ without the reader starts at $10^{-10}$ for the density and pressure floors
({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.hpp EquationOfStateOptionsImpl >}}). Refused: any key other than `type`,
`gammad`, `weight`, `density-floor`, `pressure-floor`, `temperature-floor`, `limiter`, `eos-file` and `verbose`.
The conserved floors are these lines
({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::apply_conserved_limiter_ >}}):

```cpp
  cons[IDN].clamp_min_(options->density_floor());
  ...
    auto min_temp = options->temperature_floor() * torch::ones_like(ke);
    auto min_ie = compute("UT->I", {cons, min_temp});
    cons[IPR].clamp_min_(ke + min_ie);
```

`ke` is the kinetic energy from the momentum raised with the cell's metric, and `compute("UT->I", ...)` reads
the already-floored density.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| this section's check | `[C1]` the two floors do not commute; `[C2]` the mass and energy a floor invents; `[C4]` the marks and the interior rule; `[C5]` the two passes floor different rows | measured, bitwise | the check's own bounds, all in `floors_check.py`. `check_C1` asserts a non-commutation above $10^{-9}$. `check_C2` asserts only a positive sign on the invented mass and energy. `check_C4` asserts exact equality of the mark booleans against the expected pattern. `check_C5` asserts exact equality against `DENSITY_FLOOR` and `PRESSURE_FLOOR`. |

: Tests of the equation-of-state limiter. {#tbl-ch08-eoslimiter-tests}

The chapter's check ports the two passes on synthetic states; it imports no snapy.[^ch08-floors-run] `[C1]`: reversing
the two conserved floors changes the energy in 2862 of 3000 random states, by up to $1.33\times10^{4}$. `[C2]`: on
4000 cells straddling the floors the passes add $4.736\times10^{-4}$ of dry mass and $1.294\times10^{2}$ of total
energy. `[C4]`: an untouched state marks nothing, a density below the floor sets the patch mark, and a NaN sets the
NaN mark. The same repair outside the interior marks nothing. `[C5]`: the primitive pass floors density
$10^{-9} \to 10^{-6}$ and pressure $10^{-9} \to 10^{-3}$ and clamps a negative fraction to 0, with no temperature
floor.

The repair cases of `test_forcing.<b>` exercise the real passes and their marks ({{< code tests/test_forcing.cpp >}});
`limiter_patch_is_reported_below_the_temperature_floor` tests floor reporting, not the non-commutation of
`[C1]`. They have not been run for this report at the pin: **pending a pinned ctest run**.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- The floors are absolute values in the deck's units. A deck whose densities are legitimately below
  $10^{-6}$ will have every cell floored, silently and on every call.
- One switch turns on this limiter, the tracer limiter, the reconstruction floors and the species
  clamps together. They cannot be selected independently, which is a design decision recorded in the
  sources, not an accident.
:::

1. **The invented mass is not tracked.** `[C2]` measures it in a synthetic state; the code keeps a
   boolean mark but no budget. A run cannot report how much mass its floors created.
2. **Open question.** Whether the energy floor should use the floored or the unfloored density is not
   discussed in any source. `[C1]` shows the choice is observable; the code makes it one way, and this
   chapter records which, not which is right.
